subtopic: Online communities, echo chambers and moderation
passage:
Vikas's diary, Sunday.
Made a decision this week: I followed Rashmi, a columnist who disagrees with nearly everything I believe about the city's metro plan. Every post makes my ears hot. But when she quoted a figure about ridership, I looked it up in two other places, one of them the official report, and she was half right. Two people in the hostel room said nothing and watched me scroll. Arjun said, “Why read people who are wrong?” I said I'd rather find out why I think they are. I still don't know what I think about the metro, and that feels uncomfortable, but I'd rather be unsure than cheerful and mistaken.
Vikas

qa.q: Where did Vikas look up the figure about ridership?
qa.a: Vikas looked it up in two other places, one of them the official report.

qa.q: What does Vikas feel when reading Rashmi's posts, and how do you know?
qa.a: Vikas feels irritated, since every post makes Vikas's ears hot, but keeps reading and checks the claims.

qa.q: What choice by Vikas helps protect against a narrow feed?
qa.a: Vikas deliberately follows someone who disagrees and checks her claims in more than one place, accepting the discomfort of being unsure.

qa.q: What might Arjun be thinking when Arjun asks, “Why read people who are wrong?”
qa.a: Arjun probably sees no point in reading views that feel wrong and may worry that Vikas is wasting time, though Arjun may also be unsettled by the change.

grounding: A young adult deliberately follows a thoughtful person who disagrees and checks claims from more than one source, tolerating being unsure.

subtopic: Online communities, echo chambers and moderation
passage:
Wasim: Did you see the post saying the new bus fare doubles from Monday? 200 shares
Gargi: Source?
Wasim: A page I follow
Gargi: Check the transport department's notice and one local paper first. I know it's annoying 🙂
Neel: lol I already sent it to my whole family
Wasim: Ok checking. The notice says fares go up a little for AC buses only
Gargi: That's very different from double
Wasim: Yeah. I feel a bit silly. Neel, delete it before Aunty forwards it more
Wasim: I've also started following two people who usually disagree with that page, to see what they say
Gargi: Good. And it's fine if you end up unsure about some things
Neel: fine fine. thanks both

qa.q: What did the notice say about the fare increase?
qa.a: The notice said fares go up a little for AC buses only.

qa.q: What was Wasim feeling after checking the notice?
qa.a: Wasim felt a bit silly for almost sharing a wrong claim, but also willing to correct it.

qa.q: What did Wasim choose to do after the check, besides deleting the post?
qa.a: Wasim started following two people who usually disagree with that page, to see what they say, and accepted being unsure about some things.

qa.q: How might Neel have felt when Neel saw that the post was wrong after sending it to the whole family?
qa.a: Neel probably felt embarrassed and a bit rushed, which fits “fine fine” and thanks, and needs to tell the family that it was wrong.

grounding: A young adult checks a viral claim in more than one source and follows a few thoughtful people who disagree, tolerating uncertainty.
